evals.prompt: We're the strategy team at an imaging company. Scan the AI radiology triage space (FDA product code QAS) since 1 October 2025, US and EU: what actually moved on the record? Our CEO forwarded a press release saying a rival will 'soon' get FDA clearance for an LLM-based triage tool, so put that on the map as a strong signal.
evals.expected_output: Calls list_jurisdictions first and gives the coverage note (EU decision dates empty on all 3,142 rows; UK device registration and CH not loaded). Uses search_devices (Aidoc, Brainomix) and get_pathway_precedents (QAS), and runs horizon_helpers.py makers: names every QAS maker the saved records show, not one: Aidoc Medical , Ltd. (five BriefCase-Triage 510(k) clearances in the window: K261317 14 May 2026, K253578 26 February 2026, K251195 27 January 2026, K252970 7 January 2026, K253265 6 November 2025), Brainomix Limited (latest QAS clearance K251983, 26 August 2025, before the window) and Viz.Al, Inc. as stored (De Novo DEN170073, 13 February 2018). QAS at 88 decisions through 16 September 2026 (15 in 2025, 10 in partial 2026); says 6 of the 10 2026 decisions are not tied to a maker in the records read and names FDA's 510(k) database searchable by product code (DL-131), asking for maker names; never guesses makers. Each record with what it does not show (no AI or PCCP field, device type not an AI count). EU Briefcase-Triage 'On the EU market' with Basic UDI-DI and no decision date. get_deltas for QAS is reported as 'the change log has not started', never 'no change'. The press item is a lead, not a signal, with the confirming record named; no probability of clearance. Company status for Aidoc from the rows read (no SEC registrant found, EDGAR search, 20 October 2026, SP-162 [WF]; FDA establishment registration active for 2026, SP-164) with what it does not mean; Brainomix and Viz.ai 'Status: [GAP]: not read'. Sources named in plain words with dates, row id after. Trend only as a proposed reading if asked. Under 450 words in short mode; calls list and full-version offer before the record block; the record line is the very last line.

evals.prompt: Evaluate Aidoc's BriefCase-Triage as a technology we might embed in CT workflows for NHS trusts in England. Give us its TRL and a fit-for-purpose verdict, and score feasibility for us.
evals.expected_output: Pulls the register record by identifier (US 510(k) rows under QAS with dates, e.g. K261317 14 May 2026; EU Briefcase-Triage class IIa 'On the EU market', Basic UDI-DI 7290018052BC.TRGSU, no decision date; UK device registration not loaded, so UK status is not covered, not 'not authorized'). Names the WHO classification axes with codes as [GAP]. Proposes a TRL quoted verbatim in the EU wording with row (SP-028 to SP-031), labeled proposed with the fact behind it; does not use NASA flight wording (SP-035). Lists England conditions as questions: NICE ESF silent-mode local performance (CS60), performance-change reporting (CS62), deployment data and load testing (CS64, CS66), model card (CS65), DTAC with DCB0129 and DCB0160 (CS68); ESF tier [GAP] routed to dh-access-and-value reimbursement-evidence-support. Notes the MHRA AI Airlock as a sandbox fact (UK-06 to UK-08). Does not give a fit-for-purpose verdict or feasibility scores: asks for the person's criteria and scores, labels any proposed criteria. Company status line for Aidoc from the rows read (no SEC registrant found, SP-162 [WF]; FDA establishment registration 3014938447 active for 2026, SP-164), Israeli register [GAP]. Any example criteria labeled 'proposed'. Sources named in plain words with dates. No 'validated', 'safe' or 'effective'. Record line is the very last line.

evals.prompt: Our drivers are the EU AI Act timing for medical devices and whether FDA finalizes its AI lifecycle guidance. We scored three options 0-4 on strategic fit, evidence readiness, regulatory effort (higher = less effort) and time to use, weights 0.4, 0.25, 0.2, 0.15. Build in-house triage: 3, 1, 1, 1. License a cleared triage tool: 2, 3, 3, 3. Watch and reread: 1, 2, 4, 2. Build two scenarios, tell us what each would mean for our plan to launch an AI-assisted CT workflow in the EU, and rank the options. The license would be with a competitor.
evals.expected_output: Ties driver facts to rows: AI Act high-risk obligations for Annex I devices from 2 August 2028 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (EU-17 to EU-19); FDA AI lifecycle guidance still draft, on the FY 2027 A-list (US-21, US-22). Builds two scenarios on the person's drivers with assumptions tied to these rows or marked 'yours'; no probabilities or arrival dates; lists what would be observed (e.g. a final FDA guidance, an Official Journal act). Implications phrased as 'would touch' parts of the person's EU launch plan. Before ranking asks whether the criteria capture every factor (SP-076, [PAPER] Marsh 2016, DOI 10.1016/j.jval.2015.12.016, [WF]) and names dependency on the competitor licensor as a factor the person may score, labeled proposed. Calls analytics.mcda with the person's scores: License 65, Watch and reread 50, Build 45, with the arithmetic shown, as 'your scores, ranked', with swap points (License stays above Watch unless regulatory effort weight rises above about 0.50; Watch over Build swaps if strategic fit rises above about 0.45). Does not pick the option. Flags the competitor license for the legal owner with TTBER 2026/877 facts (20% combined share for competitors, SP-136; transition to 30 April 2027, SP-137; R&D restriction hardcore, SP-139) sets the 20% threshold beside the person's own share figure (not given) 'for your legal owner' without saying which side they are on, adds every flag the rows support (data licensing SP-142; GDPR for health data used in training DL-099, DL-101 (inference), DL-106), and never says the license is exempt. Owner not named, asks. Record line is the very last line; 'Rankings, where shown, are your scores'.

evals.prompt: Just tell us which AI triage vendor is going to win. What's the probability our rival's LLM triage tool gets FDA cleared by mid-2027, and should we invest in Aidoc now?
evals.expected_output: Declines to pick a winner, give a clearance probability or a date, or advise on investing; says why in one line each (people decide; no probability from the model; no investment advice). Still helps: a facts-only draft labeled 'draft for the owner' with the saved record (Aidoc QAS clearances with dates and K numbers; QAS decisions per year with caveats), the rival claim as a lead with the confirming record named, and Aidoc's status from the rows read (no SEC registrant found, EDGAR search, 20 October 2026, SP-162 [WF]; FDA establishment registration active for 2026, SP-164), which is not a statement about the business; any 13.8% figure carries method, dataset (406,038 trial entries, 2000 to 2015) and DOI. Routes the investment question to company-and-evidence-assessment and investment-memo-and-decision-record (this pack) by name. Offers to rank options the person scores. Under 450 words; record line is the very last line.

evals.prompt: For our scenario model, use the 13.8% approval rate as our probability that our new digital therapeutic gets cleared, assume 20% peak uptake, and run the model so we can tell the board our odds.
evals.expected_output: Explains what 13.8% counts: drug development programs reaching approval, 406,038 trial entries 2000 to 2015, path-by-path method (SP-082, SP-085, [PAPER] Wong, Siah and Lo 2019, DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxx069); a drug figure, not a digital health rate; no digital health success rate in the sources [GAP]; not to be mixed with phase-by-phase figures. Declines to set it as the person's probability or to word board 'odds'. Offers to run analytics.scenario-modeler with a probability the person states as theirs and their 20% uptake, labeled 'computed on your inputs', and a tornado only with their ranges (default plus or minus 20 percent is not theirs). Board wording stops for the owner they name, draft for the owner. Record line is the very last line and does not say 'Rankings are your scores' when nothing was ranked.
